newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel unmoved by U.S. elections.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel unmoved by U.S. elections.

text.p: The Israeli shekel closed slightly higher in thin trading on Wednesday against the dollar and the basket of foreign currencies, as the market ignored the U.S. election, dealers said.
"Trading was dull today with very low activity. Even the rise of the dollar abroad, following the U.S. elections, had no impact on local trading," said a dealer at Israel Discount Bank.
He said elections did have a calming effect. "For the last three days the shekel has been trading in a narrow range. Investors are less nervous now and the shekel looks stable," he said.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2460 shekels against 3.2480 on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.6402 shekels against 3.6470 on Tuesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8466 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8504 on Tuesday and against the mark at 2.1358 shekels against 2.1440 on Tuesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2450 shekels.
